trial.ground_truth: Notification consumer pauses processing and commits
trial.predicted_root_cause: notification-service's Kafka consumer has stopped consuming from redpanda partition 0. Across three snapshots the group committed_offset stayed frozen at 33150 while end_offset advanced (33243 → 33289 → 33352), so lag grew monotonically 93 → 139 → 202 entirely from producer writes; consumer_rps was 0.0. HTTP health stays green (200, healthy), pool-stats show 0 waiting/1 queued, and in-window notification-service logs contain only /pool-stats self-probes with no consumer or poll errors. This pattern indicates a silently blocked or dead consumer loop — not a crash (no errors), not slow processing (committed offset would still advance), and not backpressure from DB/Redis pools (no waiting). Producer side (order-service checkout) continues normally with healthy HTTP latency and 0% errors, so the impact is isolated to asynchronous notification delivery.

regression_risks: Restart may replay uncommitted messages if processing is non-idempotent; notifications INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING suggests dedup intent but is not verified as sufficient.
Stall could recur silently after restart since root mechanism is unchanged; HTTP health checks still cannot detect commit-age/lag growth.
Added consumer liveness/commit-age alerting risks false positives during legitimate rebalances, backfills, or low-traffic idle periods.
critic_result.test_sufficiency: Sufficient for the stated scope: four offset snapshots establish a monotone frozen-commit trend, pool-stats and Redis deltas refute the named alternatives, and post-recovery lag=0 with notification DB writes demonstrates relief. Insufficient to pin the in-loop mechanism (no consumer logs; services/app.py out of scope) or to claim durable production fix — recovery was operator-performed, no code change tested.
critic_result.verification_summary: Offset evidence is internally consistent and cumulative: committed_offset pinned at 33150 across four snapshots while end_offset rose 33243→33289→33352→33490, giving lag 93→139→202→340; consumer_rps 0.0 (E-c807f2631c3340c7), producer_rps ~3.65. Topology (E-70e751cc70ad4436, E-1b35fd0cdb1d495a) confirms a redpanda→notification-service edge, so an uncommitted consumer group is plausible and the diagnosis correctly localizes impact to async notification delivery. Correct discriminations: not slow processing (committed offset would advance), not DB/Redis backpressure — pool-stats show requests_waiting 0 (E-a4bc2324e42b41d4), and Redis hits/misses are explicitly cumulative so cannot evidence active cache pressure (E-44aa6b08b02147b8 vs E-ea34cbaf735c42eb). The strongest support is the recurrence/relief pattern: lag was 340 pre-recovery and 0 (committed=end=33596) post-recovery (E-a1fef7547c9c4410), plus notification-service INSERT INTO notifications in after-window DB activity, and notification-service's first new log? (existing logs contain only /pool-stats self-probes, E-298643ff97254e13). Limits: the specific stall mechanism is unproven (no poll error log; consumer loop in services/app.py outside allowlisted scope, E-c1608c17f7cb48c2). Recovery was operator-driven; this verifies the diagnosis and operational remediation, not a production deployment or an AI patch (patch_decision NO_CODE_PATCH, not_an_ai_repair=true).

judgment.explanation: The diagnosis correctly identifies the CONSUMER_LAG scenario on notification-service: the Kafka consumer on redpanda partition 0 is stalled, with committed_offset frozen at 33150 while end_offset advances and lag grows monotonically (93→139→202). The affected service, category, and causal mechanism (consumer not consuming/committing causing backlog) materially match the ground truth. Evidence is strong: three independent inspect_kafka snapshots (E-4a7d0f551bd64a6c, E-69a8d3ec3d034e51, E-3a6a182ee6d94ab6) independently corroborate frozen committed offsets and rising lag, with notification-service in-window logs showing only /pool-stats self-probes. The diagnosis rules out alternative causes (crash, slow processing, pool backpressure) appropriately and recommends operational recovery to drain the backlog, consistent with ground truth. The higher-level mechanism is accurate even without specifying the exact injection implementation.
